name: Pan-Islamism
summary: Pan-Islamism seeks the political unity of Muslims, under one Islamic state or caliphate or at least a common international body, on the basis of religion instead of ethnicity or nation. It arose in the late 19th century as a response to European imperial domination and Ottoman decline, and rejects nationalism as divisive. Advocates generally want sharia to shape public life and see Muslim solidarity as the main defence against foreign domination.
scope: The mainstream Sunni tradition from Jamal al-Din al-Afghani and Muhammad Abduh's Al-Urwa al-Wuthqa (1884) through Abdul Hamid II's Ottoman policy and Rashid Rida's caliphate writings, plus the state-level form in the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation charter. Shia variants such as Khomeini's, and the violent jihadist strands, are not the basis. Economic and social-policy statements the movement never addressed are inferred at low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Jamal al-Din al-Afghani
keyFigures.role: Early advocate of Muslim unity against European imperialism, co-founder of Al-Urwa al-Wuthqa.

keyFigures.name: Rashid Rida
keyFigures.role: Salafi reformer who made restoring the caliphate and sharia the path to Muslim unity.

keyFigures.name: Abdul Hamid II
keyFigures.role: Ottoman sultan who promoted pan-Islamism as state policy in the late 19th century.

sources.usedFor: State-level pan-Islamist commitments: Islamic solidarity, sovereignty, Palestine, Muslim minorities, development, democracy and human rights.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a pan-Islamist concern; inferred from the OIC's stated aim of sustained socio-economic development and Islamic values of justice and welfare, which fit state-backed care.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Pan-Islamists did not address wage law; Rida's view that a sharia-abiding society would reject both capitalism and class socialism gives no clear direction on wage floors.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Rida saw sharia as resisting capitalism, yet pan-Islamist programs such as Erbakan's and the OIC's favour trade and integration, so adherents are split.

public-ownership.rationale: No pan-Islamist text takes a position on nationalising utilities; Rida's rejection of both capitalism and socialism leaves the question open.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Zakat is a duty on wealth, but pan-Islamism has no program on progressive taxation, so this is not placed.

unions-good.rationale: The movement is about the ummah, not labour organisation; Rida's rejection of class-based politics cuts against it, but nothing is stated.

property-fundamental.rationale: Islamic law protects private property and Rida's sharia order rejects socialism, but pan-Islamists did not make property rights a central theme; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not addressed by pan-Islamist writers; no defining stance can be inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed directly; Islamic values of solidarity and zakat, which the OIC charter invokes alongside social development, make welfare cuts an unlikely stance.

worker-ownership.rationale: Rida opposed class-based socialism as inconsistent with sharia, so collective worker ownership is not part of the program; inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Pan-Islamism has no doctrine on surveillance; Muslim states pursuing it have generally supported security measures while Islamist opposition suffered surveillance, so adherents split.

legalize-drugs.rationale: A sharia-based order of the kind Rida advocated prohibits intoxicants, so adherents oppose legalising recreational drugs.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The OIC pushes for laws against defamation of Islam but also champions human rights and freedoms; pan-Islamists are split on a general hate-speech law.

strong-leader.rationale: Afghani favoured replacing lax rulers with strong, patriotic men and revolution from above, and a caliph is a unifying authority; strong leadership is welcomed, not gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: Pan-Islamism seeks to build a unified Islamic state or caliphate, so it regards the state as necessary and positive.

limit-guns.rationale: The movement has no gun policy; this is inferred as indifferent.

empower-police-military.rationale: Afghani and Rida stressed military and technological strength to resist imperial domination, implying more capable armed forces; inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Rida's sharia-centred order forbids extramarital sex and so rules out legalising prostitution.

decide-locally.rationale: Pan-Islamism aims at centralised unity of Muslims under one state or body and treats local fragmentation as weakness, though it tolerates member-state sovereignty in practice.

rehabilitation.rationale: Sharia penal law is central to the program, but the movement did not take a stance on rehabilitation versus punishment as a general aim.

traditional-family.rationale: Rida and sharia-based Islamism treat the Islamic family order as the base of a moral community; the OIC charter likewise aims to inculcate Islamic values in children and youth.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Sharia-based advocates such as Rida reject same-sex unions as contrary to Islamic law.

abortion-legal.rationale: Mainstream Islamic law restricts abortion, particularly after ensoulment; inferred from the sharia emphasis rather than stated in pan-Islamist texts.

more-religion-public.rationale: Pan-Islamism seeks a polity grounded in Islamic principles, and Rida wanted sharia to govern public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Pan-Islamism rejects race as a basis of identity but has no program on redress of racial injustice.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Sharia-based adherents see gender roles as divinely ordained rather than social; inferred, as the question is modern.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Pan-Islamism rejects nationalism in favour of the ummah, but wants to preserve Islamic heritage; the OIC charter speaks of preserving Islamic symbols and common heritage, not national culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Afghani favoured revolution from above and urgent revival, while Abduh favoured gradual reform; the mainstream emphasis is on rapid restoration of unity.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Pan-Islamism treats Muslims as one community across borders, so restricting movement of Muslims is at odds with it; inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Pan-Islamists want strong Muslim-world bodies like the OIC, and the charter backs the UN, yet distrust Western-dominated global bodies; the answer splits by institution.

free-trade.rationale: Erbakan's pan-Islamist plan envisioned economic integration of Muslim states like the EU, but with Muslim-only blocs rather than general free trade; inferred.

nation-first.rationale: Pan-Islamism is an anti-nationalist movement that puts the ummah above the nation-state.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Rida backed jihad against European influence and Zionism, but pan-Islamists see Western intervention as imperial pretext; inferred scepticism.

open-borders.rationale: The goal of a single Muslim polity implies free movement among Muslim lands, but not open borders generally; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Afghani urged Muslims to adopt modern science and technology to resist the West, which favours growth; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The OIC charter mentions preserving the environment for future generations, but pan-Islamism has no position on drastic climate policy.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Afghani urged adopting Western science and technology for strength but saw Islam, not technology, as the mobilising creed.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; Muslim states pursue it for strength, but there is no doctrinal stance.

revolution-justified.rationale: Afghani sought revolution to replace foreign-aligned rulers, and Rida endorsed armed jihad against imperial rule, though state-backed pan-Islamism under Abdul Hamid II was conservative.

experts-over-public.rationale: Rida gave authority to scholars on sharia but did not generalise to experts in policy; adherents differ.

central-planning.rationale: Pan-Islamists did not endorse planning; Rida rejected capitalism and socialism alike.

socialized-markets.rationale: No pan-Islamist position on enterprise ownership; Rida rejected both capitalism and socialism.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Islamic inheritance law prescribes fixed shares among heirs, which a sharia-minded adherent would not override with heavy inheritance taxation; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; zakat provides a religious welfare tradition but no unconditional income is advocated.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Pan-Islamists focus on bloc integration; no stance on tariffs is documented.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Erbakan's pan-Islamist plan used joint economic and technological projects among Muslim states, but no doctrine on state investment direction exists.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Rida rejected class-based socialism, so abolition of money and wages has no place in the program; inferred.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Erbakan proposed a common currency for Muslim states, which implies central institutions but gives no view on abolition.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: No pan-Islamist text addresses state-recognised bodies setting wages.

one-party-rule.rationale: Pan-Islamism puts religion, not a party, as the guide of the state; movements such as Hizb ut-Tahrir are parties but do not call for a single-party state; inferred.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Abdul Hamid II's Ottoman sultan-caliphate promoted pan-Islamism and Rida backed Ibn Saud, so adherents accept monarchical rule that upholds Islam.

democracy-best.rationale: Rida called democracy a colonial deceit and Afghani doubted parliamentary government for Muslim lands; later Islamist variants accept shura as a substitute.

direct-votes.rationale: Pan-Islamists put sharia above popular votes, so direct lawmaking by citizens is not endorsed; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Rida opposed class-based socialism and held sharia to be the basis of political order, not councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Abdul Hamid II used pan-Islamism partly to prevent secession of Muslim peoples, and the movement seeks unification rather than fragmentation.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rida held the caliph should be a qualified Muslim, even Arab, but pan-Islamism does not claim natural rulers in a general sense.

political-violence-never.rationale: Rida supported armed jihad to expel European influence, so adherents reject an absolute ban on political violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: The Islamic Golden Age is romanticised as a strong era, but no text says war builds national character.

separate-church-state.rationale: Pan-Islamism seeks a state based on Islamic principles and Rida considered government not adhering to sharia apostasy.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Advocates held that returning to sharia would make Muslims united and strong again, as Rida argued in his writings on the caliphate.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Rida's caliphate and sharia order centres justice and defence in the Islamic state.

military-superiority.rationale: Afghani sought Muslim strength against the West, which implies military capability, but the aim is collective rather than national superiority; inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Pan-Islamism bases identity on religion, not ethnicity or race, and rejects nationalism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rida's circle opposed class-based socialism; pan-Islamism sees imperial domination and Muslim disunity as the central issues.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Rida rejected class-based socialism; Islamic inheritance and property norms accept inequality of outcome.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: No pan-Islamist source discusses indigenous land claims, and the movement's focus on the ummah gives nothing to infer from.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-imperialism is core, and Afghani opposed European domination, but reparations as a demand are not documented; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: The central aim is to unite Muslims under one state or an international body based on Islamic principles.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Islamic ethics set community and divine duty above self-interest, and the ummah is the object of loyalty.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Sharia-centred political thought stresses duties to God and community; the OIC charter qualifies human rights by member states' legal systems.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The OIC charter mentions preserving the environment, but pan-Islamism has no doctrine on nature's intrinsic worth.

limit-population.rationale: No pan-Islamist program for population control; Islamic family values and calls for Muslim strength suggest opposition; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Afghani urged adopting Western technology and science, so industrial civilisation is not rejected wholesale.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Afghani called for modern science to resist the West, but pan-Islamists subordinate technology to Islam rather than welcome disruption of institutions.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; Rida's scripturalism suggests suspicion of altering human nature; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; sharia-based authority rests on scholars and the caliph, not algorithms.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Pan-Islamist writers of the 19th and 20th centuries never addressed digital privacy, so no stance can be inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement draws on early Islam and the Golden Age as models of unified Muslim power and seeks to restore the caliphate, though it also embraces modern means.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Pan-Islamism is explicitly principle-driven: Rida held governance must follow sharia regardless of expedience.

direct-action.rationale: Afghani agitated by journal, travel and plots, while Abduh favoured education; adherents split between action and institutions.

means-match-ends.rationale: No doctrine linking means and ends is stated.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Afghani sought modern strength for Muslims, so a return to foraging is foreign to the ideology; inferred.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not part of the program; Rida opposed socialism.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Rida's sharia economy rests on property, zakat and inheritance rules, not pure need-based distribution; inferred.

production-for-use.rationale: Neither Afghani nor Rida framed economics as production for use or profit; Rida rejected both capitalism and socialism, so adherents are indifferent.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Rida rejected class-based socialism, so profit as exploitation is not a pan-Islamist thesis, though interest is condemned in Islamic law.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rida opposed class-based socialism and held that sharia, not a class, should rule.

collective-farming.rationale: Not a pan-Islamist theme, and Rida opposed socialism; inferred.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Pan-Islamists blame European imperialism for domination of Muslims, but not capitalism as a system.

taxation-theft.rationale: Zakat and state revenue are part of an Islamic state under sharia, so taxation is legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: Sharia-based government restricts conduct on religious grounds beyond harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Pan-Islamism puts the ummah as a collective object of loyalty and its identity above the individual.

conscription.rationale: The movement stresses Muslim strength vs imperial powers, and Muslim states such as the Ottoman Empire used conscription; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The movement binds Muslims to a shared polity and does not see exit as a main check.

state-as-business.rationale: Pan-Islamism sees the state as a religious and moral community, not a business.

positive-liberty.rationale: The movement speaks of freedom from foreign domination rather than material means to act, so this philosophical claim is not addressed.

media-academia-power.rationale: Rida condemned Western ideas but made no claim about media-academic power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The movement rejects race as basis of identity and unites Muslims of all ethnicities.

organic-representation.rationale: Rida valued shura but gave no program for corporate representation.

total-state.rationale: Sharia is broad in scope but pan-Islamism did not call for state direction of culture and economy as a totalitarian program.

national-rebirth.rationale: The movement sees Muslims as in decline from a Golden Age and seeks revival, but of the ummah rather than a nation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Pan-Islamism seeks unification of Muslim lands, which can imply expansion, but is framed as defence against imperialism; adherents split.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Pan-Islamists rely on the bay'a (oath) tradition for the caliph, but not feudal personal loyalties; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Not part of any pan-Islamist program.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Rida criticised Western ideas, but no claim is stated about knowledge and power.

universal-morality.rationale: Afghani held Islam and its law compatible with reason, and the OIC speaks of the universality of the Islamic religion; adherents see Islamic moral truths as universal.

single-common-good.rationale: Rida's shura and sharia order aims at one divinely ordered good for the community, not balancing interest groups.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Rida opposed Zionism, and the OIC charter supports Palestinian self-determination with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as capital.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed by pan-Islamist texts; the OIC charter supports Palestinians' rights but not a general diaspora principle.

revive-national-language.rationale: Pan-Islamism opposes nationalism, though Rida stressed Arab leadership; revival of national languages as state languages is not a theme.

workplace-democracy.rationale: No pan-Islamist text discusses how companies should be governed, and the program is silent on the issue.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education policy appears only as the OIC's aim of Islamic upbringing; school funding mechanisms are not addressed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Pan-Islamist writers gave no view on fiscal policy; Islamic opposition to interest-bearing debt is not tied to deficit spending.

economic-freedom.rationale: Not addressed; Rida rejected capitalism but also socialism.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed; pan-Islamists emphasise sharia as law rather than merely rulers' example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Pan-Islamism rejects the nation as the unit, though the OIC charter respects member states' self-determination and Palestinian self-determination; mixed in practice.

force-without-un.rationale: The OIC charter upholds the UN Charter, but pan-Islamists distrust Western-dominated bodies; split.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Rida prioritised revelation over reason and Islam is the mobilising creed; Afghani tried to reconcile the two but did not subordinate faith.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; solidarity among Muslims across borders makes citizenship tests foreign to the doctrine.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditionality is not a pan-Islamist topic; zakat traditions do not settle the question for the modern state.

class-collaboration.rationale: Rida rejected class-based politics, and pan-Islamists treat Muslims as one community.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The OIC charter calls for preserving Islamic symbols and common heritage; revival of past glory is a motif.

dominated-front.rationale: Muslim unity against imperial domination is the founding aim, as in Afghani's anti-British Al-Urwa al-Wuthqa and Rida's anti-imperialism.

workers-nation.rationale: Pan-Islamism opposes both national and class lines of organisation, preferring the ummah.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Sharia-based advocates hold distinct roles for men and women; the OIC charter qualifies women's rights by member states' laws.

ban-interest.rationale: Islamic law prohibits riba and sharia-minded pan-Islamists follow it; Rida held sharia society resists capitalism.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The movement rejects race as a basis for identity and unites Muslims of all races.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Rida rejected class-based analysis, so the state is not seen as a ruling-class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not addressed; Saudi-led pan-Islamism benefited from oil but has no doctrine.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; Muslim unity over national culture cuts against assimilation, though Islamic norms are expected.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not part of the ideology; its conspiracy narratives concern imperial powers rather than demographics.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral system design is not addressed, since the movement is more concerned with unity than with parliamentary mechanics.

national-mission.rationale: The OIC speaks of the universality of Islam and Islam's pioneering role, but the mission belongs to the ummah rather than a country.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Sharia-based adherents deny structural male advantage as framed in modern feminist terms; inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not part of the program; Islamic family values oppose it; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The OIC charter promotes rule of law and accountability, but adherents split over past abuses by Muslim states.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Pan-Islamism calls for a state or caliphate with sharia and wide religious functions, not a minimal one.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The ummah unites Muslims of all ethnicities and rejects race as basis.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The OIC charter invokes Islamic values of equality, justice and human dignity, though classical sharia differentiates by religion and sex.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Rida opposed Zionism and the OIC supports Palestinians' rights under occupation, consistent with viewing Israel as a colonial project; the exact framing is inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: A sharia-based order applies religious law and not a single secular civil code.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Rida held that leaving Islam is apostasy; restrictions on conversion are consistent with this though not a pan-Islamist theme.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Islamic practice permits cattle slaughter, so adherents oppose a ban.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The OIC charter calls for inculcating Islamic values in youth through education; adherents favour religious instruction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This is a Marxist-Leninist question about socialist states and has no counterpart in pan-Islamist writing.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Rida held shura is basic but rejected democracy as a colonial deceit; legitimacy rests on sharia compliance, with consultation, so adherents split.

trade-surplus.rationale: Export-import balance is not addressed by pan-Islamist thinkers, whose economic ideas centre on Muslim-bloc integration.

population-transfer.rationale: Not stated; the OIC charter supports Muslim minorities' dignity and Palestinian rights, and unity ideology opposes expulsions of Muslims; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Rida supported armed jihad to expel European influence, so initiating force is not always wrong.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The movement stresses unity and solidarity, not struggle among peoples, as the engine of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; many Islamist movements have been banned themselves, but adherents also back state security.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Anti-imperial freedom from foreign domination is central, but this republican concept is not stated.

separated-powers.rationale: Rida valued shura but gave no doctrine on separation of powers.

vanguard-party.rationale: Pan-Islamists see the ummah and scholars as agents; Hizb ut-Tahrir uses a party but Rida's tradition does not stress a vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Zakat is a pillar and the OIC speaks of development and justice, but no pan-Islamist priority is stated.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy question never touched by pan-Islamist writers, so no position is inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour law is not a pan-Islamist concern, and no source states a position on strike rules.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not stated; Islamic tradition ties poverty to injustice and unequal distribution.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The ummah is explicitly multi-ethnic, so ethnic diversity within Islam is not seen as divisive.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sharia-based advocates favour qualified office holders such as the caliph and scholars, not lottery.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price fixing in scarcity is not discussed in the pan-Islamist sources; classical Islamic jurists were divided on it.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Pan-Islamist texts do not discuss emergency powers, and adherents in different states have both supported and suffered them.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not addressed; Rida used the press as his own tool but also favoured moral censorship.

party-commands-army.rationale: The caliph or head of the Islamic state commands, not a party; inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Muslims as members of one community would not face long waits; inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of elected officials is not addressed by pan-Islamist thinkers, so the answer is neutral.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party organisation is not a theme of the movement, whose main vehicles are states, scholars and the press.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Pan-Islamism seeks to unite Muslim states, including through EU-like bodies such as Erbakan's D8 and the OIC, pooling sovereignty in a Muslim union.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Rida's caliph holds supreme authority, including military command, though ministers' selection is not detailed.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not applicable to Islam, which has no bishops.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rida valued scholars' authority over sharia, while Khomeini's variant called for rule of a jurist; Sunni strands leave authority to a caliph advised by scholars, so adherents differ in degree.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Pan-Islamism calls for unity and loyalty to the ummah, not working for defeat of one's government.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Sharia-minded adherents accept moral limits on art; inferred from Rida's scripturalism.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; a caliph traditionally holds office for life.

recall-officials.rationale: Not addressed; Rida's shura tradition allows deposing an unjust ruler but gives no mechanism.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Pan-Islamists opposed foreign alliances with Western powers and foreign bases, though states like Saudi Arabia hold such alliances; adherents split but doctrine leans against.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Islamic law permits rent, so adherents oppose prohibition.

people-in-arms.rationale: Rida endorsed jihad, but nothing is stated about replacing professional armies.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Pan-Islamists did not contrast rural and urban virtue, so there is nothing to infer from their writing.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Pan-Islamism seeks the unity of Muslims divided by colonial borders, though the nation concerned is the ummah.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Rida and Afghani were themselves educated reformers, and the sources show no stance on this popular grievance.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Rida condemned Western ideas and the OIC speaks of the universality of Islam, so adherents do not treat all civilizations as equal.

death-penalty.rationale: Sharia penal law includes capital punishment and Rida held sharia must govern.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Sharia-minded adherents oppose secular gender-equality curricula; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Afghani rejected Darwin's account of human origins and held that humans have souls; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Sharia-based morality prohibits it, and Rida's order would enforce it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Pan-Islamism bases belonging on faith not descent, so descent-only citizenship is not endorsed; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed; unity under Islam is more important than language.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The OIC charter supports Muslim minorities' religious identity abroad, but pan-Islamists apply sharia at home; split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Pan-Islamism stresses communal unity and conformity to Islamic norms; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not stated; the OIC charter seeks equality in the global economy and the movement is anti-imperial; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Afghani linked freedom from imperial domination to technological and institutional strength; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Rida favoured a sharia constitution, not necessarily an elected assembly; split.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Afghani favoured strong rulers for modernisation, but no stated stance on growth trade-offs.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Zakat and Islamic solidarity favour aid, and the OIC emphasises socio-economic development, but the focus is Muslim peoples.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Pan-Islamist strength aims support independent capability, but no source states this; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Rida's caliph is chosen by those who bind and loose, not by direct popular election; inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Afghani and Rida condemned lax, foreign-aligned rulers as the cause of Muslim decline, and Afghani urged replacing them with strong, patriotic men.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Pan-Islamists never addressed monetary institutions; Rida's rejection of both capitalism and class socialism gives no clear direction, so adherents are treated as split.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from Rida's opposition to Zionism and the OIC's commitment to Palestine and Jerusalem; low because OIC states have themselves backed land-for-peace formulas.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Inferred from Rida's view that a sharia-abiding society rejects unrestrained capitalism, and from the OIC's stress on Islamic values of justice and welfare.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Pan-Islamists opposed Marxist atheism but did not analyse the Soviet economy; nothing in the sources gives a position on how to classify it.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Pan-Islamists never addressed environmental regulation, and stewardship values give no clear direction on acting under uncertainty.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from the call for Muslim solidarity against foreign domination and the OIC's commitment to common support among members.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The OIC charter and Rida's opposition to Zionism treat Palestine and Jerusalem as occupied land whose seizure is illegitimate regardless of time.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Pan-Islamists want sharia to shape public life and the religious establishment to keep its authority, so they reject placing clergy under a secular state.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from the caliph as a unifying figure of the whole ummah, though Rida's caliph also held real religious and political authority.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from the OIC's stress on sovereignty and territorial integrity of members and the movement's hostility to Muslim fragmentation.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from the Ottoman model of a caliphate over diverse lands with local legal traditions, and the OIC's respect for member sovereignty within a loose union.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Sunni pan-Islamists see the caliph as chosen by consultation and bound by sharia, with no divine descent.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure was not a pan-Islamist concern; zakat is a flat proportion but Rida's rejection of both capitalism and socialism gives no clear direction on income tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: Afghani and Abduh stressed education and reform to renew Muslims, but Islamic teaching on innate disposition (fitra) balances this, so adherents are not clearly on one side.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Pan-Islamists hold that rulers, including the caliph, are bound by sharia and by consultation.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no principle points clearly either way.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Afghani favoured constitutional, consultative rule and Rida shura, but neither framed it as a blend of few and many, so this is inferred and unclear.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from the Islamic objection to glorifying any human, although Abdul Hamid II's court cultivated the sultan's image.

equal-parenting.rationale: Inferred from traditional sharia custody norms, which pan-Islamists did not seek to revise.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Pan-Islamism puts religious unity above class division and rejects socialist class doctrine; inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not a pan-Islamist concern; adherents have no settled view.

refugee-return.rationale: The OIC charter commits to the Palestinian cause and the rights of displaced Muslims.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Pan-Islamism rejects nationalism as divisive, so claims based on nationality are opposed.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Rida's sharia-centred caliphate writings imply penalties for leaving the faith, though not stated in these sources; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Rida and sharia-minded pan-Islamists favour modest-dress norms; inferred, not stated.

common-currency.rationale: Muslim economic integration under the OIC and caliphate ideal fits a shared currency; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Union is by faith, not language family or ancestry, so an ethnic basis is disfavoured; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred as no settled view.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The OIC charter calls for protecting the rights and dignity of Muslim minorities in the countries where they live.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Afghani and Rida argued that faith, reason and moral unity drive Muslim revival, not material conditions alone.

ban-cartels.rationale: No stated position; inferred as split.

no-bailouts.rationale: No stated position; inferred as split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Rida held that sharia and shura bind rulers, so majority rule does not override it; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Rida's sharia-based social views imply distinct gender roles over quotas; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Muslim solidarity against foreign domination favours cooperation among Muslim states and less dependence on outsiders; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: No stated position; inferred as split.

moral-incentives.rationale: Afghani's call for Muslim moral renewal suggests duty-based motivation; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Mainstream pan-Islamism works through states, the caliphate and the OIC, not armed vanguards; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The caliphate and Ottoman sultanate it favoured were hereditary or sacral offices, though Afghani backed constitutionalism; inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred: pan-Islamists put the Muslim community at the centre of identity, so teaching history from an Islamic civilizational standpoint fits, though no text addresses school curricula.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Afghani's and Rida's pan-Islamism was driven by resistance to European imperial rule over Muslim lands, so a claim of rightful tutelage is rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred: pan-Islamists reject nationalism, so pride in nation, flag and anthem is disfavoured, but loyalty to Islam and the community is encouraged, which splits the statement.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred: pan-Islamists stress unity of believers across races, but the admissions policy was never addressed.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred: not a pan-Islamist concern; Rida's rejection of both capitalism and class socialism gives no direction on how money is created.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Inferred: pan-Islamists saw Western economic domination as a threat to Muslims but did not hold a theory of capitalist collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred: the Ottoman pan-Islamism of Abdul Hamid II sought influence among Muslim peoples across the empire, and the OIC cultivates ties across Muslim states, so the idea fits.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred: pan-Islamists want Muslim solidarity and economic cooperation among Muslim states, which resembles regional integration rather than delinking, and the OIC charter stresses development.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: the thesis is a Marxist one and pan-Islamism did not address class; it does stress exploitation by foreign powers, which gives no clear direction.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred: pan-Islamists want sharia to shape public life and stress Muslim solidarity, so a general licence to discriminate on any grounds runs against their communal ethic.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred: Afghani favoured constitutionalism, but Rida held sharia to be supreme over human law, so an entrenched charter is only partly their model; the OIC charter lists human rights as a goal.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Pan-Islamists see colonial partition of Muslim lands as imperial imposition and call for Muslim unity against it.

elective-rulers.rationale: Afghani backed constitutionalism and Rida shura and consultation of the community in choosing the caliph.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on community unity over individual or group vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Afghani called for resisting despotic rulers and urged constitutional limits on them.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Rida held that sharia is the supreme law, with shura subordinate to it.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from the Islamic ethic of kindness to animals; not a pan-Islamist theme.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from Islamic law allowing animal use under rules of mercy.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from the OIC's stated Islamic values of justice and welfare and the zakat tradition.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Afghani and Rida were political activists who held that Muslims must act politically to resist domination.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from the critique of European cultural domination; not a developed theory.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from the same critique of cultural influence on Muslim elites; no explicit source.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Afghani denounced European exploitation of Muslim countries' wealth and resources.

native-born-offices.rationale: Pan-Islamism puts religion above nationality and rejects nationalism, so offices tied to birth in one nation do not fit.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred from the OIC charter's stress on sovereignty and non-interference.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from the pan-Islamic aim of mutual reliance among Muslim countries over dependence on foreign powers.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The OIC charter commits to restoring occupied territories, notably Palestine and Al-Quds.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the OIC's support for the native Palestinian population's sovereignty.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from the preference for sharia-based rather than Western secular constitutional values.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Not addressed; pan-Islamists reject the Western equivalence framing, inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; inferred acceptance of the mainstream historical view.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the reformist rejection of shrine veneration and the anti-colonial hostility to its symbols.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents have no clear position.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from traditional gender roles; no explicit position.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Afghani and Rida held that Muslims should build a polity on Islamic principles and not copy European institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from the caliphate model of rule by consultation and law, not army guardianship.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed; the OIC charter supports women's advancement without a stance on paid domestic work.

filial-duty.rationale: Not a pan-Islamist theme as such; inferred from the Islamic duty to honour and support parents that Islamic reformers took for granted.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: the pan-Islamist ideal of leaders chosen through consultation (shura) by notables, as Rida argued, rather than by examination alone.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from the movement's anti-imperialism and defence of sovereignty against foreign economic domination.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Adherents are split: Islamic law lets a husband end a marriage without proving fault and a wife seek release by agreement, but reformers resist Western-style liberalisation of family law; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Rida's shura works through notables who advise the caliph, not delegates under binding instruction and recall; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from Islamic emphasis on communal solidarity and welfare, which sits poorly with purely private pension saving.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from Islamic law, which recognises private ownership of land, so common tenure conditional on use is not its norm.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Afghani backed constitutional, consultative government and Rida shura; a budget needing parliamentary approval is inferred from that.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred: pan-Islamism unites Arabs, Turks, Persians and others in one community, so enforcing a single state language runs against its multi-ethnic aim.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Rida's opposition to Zionist land acquisition and the anti-imperialist concern to keep Muslim lands out of foreign hands.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred: equal standing of believers under sharia is its norm, whereas judging policy by group outcomes is a modern Western egalitarian idea.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from the movement's critique of European materialism and its stress on Islamic moral restraint.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Violent jihadist strands are excluded from scope; the OIC charter stresses non-interference in members' internal affairs; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The OIC charter respects member sovereignty and non-interference, and unity is sought through solidarity, not force; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from the anti-European stance and Rida's rejection of capitalism.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the OIC charter's commitment to state sovereignty and from resistance to foreign domination.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred: a movement seeking a large, strong Muslim community would favour a higher birth rate.

job-guarantee.rationale: Not addressed; economic policy is not a pan-Islamist concern.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed; the OIC charter backs democracy among members while Rida was sceptical, so adherents split.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: Rida held that sharia is the source of binding authority, not law as such.

non-intervention.rationale: The OIC charter stresses non-interference, though adherents also support Muslim solidarity in defence of Muslim lands.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Rida opposed Zionism and similar conspiracy claims appear among adherents, but they are not a defining tenet.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from Rida's insistence on sharia as the basis of society, including family law.

local-production.rationale: Not addressed; economic cooperation among Muslim states is stressed over local self-sufficiency.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred: unity is pursued through states, the caliphate and bodies like the OIC, not informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred: adherents want a supranational Muslim body, though the OIC charter respects national sovereignty.

religious-nation.rationale: Pan-Islamism bases political unity on religion rather than ethnicity or nation, and rejects nationalism.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: pan-Islamists would honour a caliph's primacy among Muslim states, but reject submission to non-Muslim powers; the statement does not separate these.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred: Muslim solidarity over national divisions suggests sharing resources across the community; the OIC stresses development cooperation.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred: pan-Islamists accept private property under sharia and do not call for common ownership of the means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred: Afghani and Rida defended religion against materialism, and Cold War Islamic solidarity bodies were anti-communist, though not a defining goal.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred: pan-Islamism never addressed how services are delivered.

religion-illusion.rationale: Pan-Islamism grounds unity in Islam as lasting truth; Afghani and Rida defend the compatibility of faith and reason, not its fading.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred: the movement resists European economic domination, though Afghani did not reject all modern commerce.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: Rida's views on women rest on sharia roles, with reform of education but not economic transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred: the family is upheld under Islamic values, and the movement has no programme of public domestic services.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: Arabic is prized as the shared language of the Muslim community, but nationalist language purging is rejected along with nationalism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: Islamic ethics honour covenants, but the movement did not address treaties with internal nations.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Pan-Islamism seeks large-scale unity under a caliphate or common body, not small communes holding property in common.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: no stated position; the OIC charter protects Muslim minorities but settlement policy is not addressed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Inferred: Pan-Islamists present Islamic solidarity and law as an alternative to Western and Marxist models, though economics was not their focus.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Muslim solidarity centers on holy places such as Jerusalem, which the OIC charter treats as a common concern; inferred for historical-religious claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not a pan-Islamist doctrine; mainstream bodies like the OIC do not endorse denial, though some adherents do; inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Traditional sharia treats same-sex relations as an offence and pan-Islamists want sharia to shape public life; the sources do not discuss it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Afghani campaigned against despotic rulers and for consultative government; the mainstream tradition did not seek to suppress opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Sharia-shaped public life implies protection of religion, though Afghani and Rida did not make blasphemy law central; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Pan-Islamism arose as a response to European imperial domination of Muslim lands and opposes it.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Afghani urged Muslims to unite and resist foreign invasion of Muslim lands, and Muslim solidarity against imperial rule is the movement's core.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Mainstream pan-Islamists such as Afghani and Rida urged reform and unity, not armed removal of rulers; violent jihadist strands are excluded from this audit.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Afghani and Abduh favored consultation (shura), but direct workplace and community decision-making is not part of the movement's program.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Pan-Islamism puts religious solidarity above lines of race and class and does not use this framework; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the traditionalist sharia orientation that pan-Islamists favor.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; classical Islamic law forbids taking life, including one's own, so this is inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Rida held that a sharia-abiding society rejects both capitalism and class socialism, taking a path beyond the usual camps.

alienated-labor.rationale: Rida's rejection of capitalism suggests sympathy for the criticism, though alienation as such is not a pan-Islamist concept; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Pan-Islamists see Islam as universal and Muslims as able to engage the West, though they stress distinct values; they would reject the claim as stated.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Rida's caliphate writings and the OIC's Islamic framing place sovereignty in God and his law.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Pan-Islamists want religion to shape public life and object to bans on Muslim dress; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic and outside the movement's concerns; no direction can be inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Rida's third way between capitalism and class socialism fits a market economy bounded by Islamic justice and welfare; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: A movement built on resisting imperial invasion and on Muslim collective defense would keep armies; inferred.

rich-first.rationale: Islamic ideas of justice and solidarity point against letting some prosper first, though the issue is not addressed; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Pan-Islamists favored Muslim unity as a power apart from the great-power blocs; the OIC has pursued a collective independent stance.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Rida argued the caliph should be chosen by consultation among qualified Muslims, not inherited, though Ottoman pan-Islamism under Abdul Hamid II used a dynastic caliphate; inferred from that tension.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Islamic law bans interest, but pan-Islamists never addressed user-owned mutual banks versus profit-sharing Islamic banks; inferred as split.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Pan-Islamism grew as resistance to foreign domination, and the OIC charter stresses sovereignty and self-determined development; inferred that lender conditions would be resisted.

property-franchise.rationale: Afghani backed constitutional, consultative government and the OIC charter backs democracy and participation; inferred that a wealth test for voting does not fit.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not a pan-Islamist concern; inferred from Rida's view that women's status is set by sharia complementarity rather than by a shared logic of domination.

reification.rationale: A Marxist-style critique of market society is absent from pan-Islamist writing, which blames imperialism and Muslim disunity; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Pan-Islamists focus on religious and anti-imperial limits on the press, not on ownership by wealth; inferred from the OIC charter's support for free expression within Islamic values.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Pan-Islamists want sharia, a fixed divine law, to govern, and Rida tied rulers to sharia and consultation, so rule by known standing law fits.

racial-franchise.rationale: Pan-Islamism bases unity on religion rather than ethnicity and rejects nationalism, so an ethnic or racial test for citizenship contradicts it.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed; adherents likely use the internet for mobilization, but its use for direct political decision is undocumented.

open-government-data.rationale: The OIC charter commits to good governance, democracy and transparency; inferred that open records fit, though the sources are silent on data publication.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Classical sharia, which pan-Islamists want to shape public life, bars Muslim women from marrying non-Muslim men; inferred from Rida's support for sharia.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The OIC charter calls for protecting minorities and tolerance, and pan-Islamism targets foreign domination, not local minorities; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not a pan-Islamist concern; inferred from its picture of unity under a caliph or shared Islamic body guided by religious scholars, with no role for citizens chosen by lot.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Afghani and Abduh urged renewed ijtihad, reasoning afresh on Islamic law to meet modern conditions and revive Muslim strength, a modernist line Rida carried on.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Not a pan-Islamist concern; the strand focused on political unity and anti-imperialism, with Islamic charity norms against hoarding but no clear position.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from traditional Islamic law, which the movement upholds; it never addressed the question.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Afghani attacked materialism and atheism as threats to Muslim solidarity and the movement makes Islam the basis of political unity.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: a movement seeking a strong caliphate or state has no tradition of abolishing policing or prisons.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; the movement favours unity of the ummah, not a settled stance on consociational arrangements.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from the Islamic emphasis on zakat and communal solidarity as the means of poor relief.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; the caliphate model by Rida has no term-limit tradition, but the OIC charter is silent.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from Rida's consultative (shura) caliphate, which has no mechanism for revocable individual delegation.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the traditional jurisprudence the movement and Rida defend, which reserves such offices to men.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from traditional Islamic family law that the movement upholds, though it never legislated on it.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The sources do not address resident aliens, though Muslim solidarity across borders suggests some openness to fellow Muslims; split and inferred.

rent-control.rationale: Not a pan-Islamist concern; Islamic values of justice are cited but no position on rent is stated; inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; pan-Islamism takes no stand against copyright, and Islamic law respects the fruits of labour; inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not part of the movement's programme; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; pan-Islamists focus on Muslim unity and not on weapons policy; inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Afghani and Abduh's Al-Urwa al-Wuthqa call on Muslims to unite against European domination of Muslim lands, which makes foreign bases a grievance.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, and positions depend on the state concerned; inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Not a pan-Islamist concern; inferred from Islamic bans on usury and the value placed on earnings from labour.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Islam permits lethal self-defence and Afghani and Rida defended armed resistance to imperial rule; inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Pan-Islamism puts the umma above nations and rejects nationalism, so it does not claim any one nation's unbroken line from antiquity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Pan-Islamists hold the binary sex of scripture and the issue never arose for them; inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Women are seen as sharing a fixed religious status and role; inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Fighting for the umma is honoured as martyrdom, but the movement rejects the nation as its unit; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Afghani framed the struggle as against imperial domination more than as a cosmic fight; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Pan-Islamists treat the umma as the people and the Hijaz and Muslim lands as a shared centre; not applicable in the statement's terms; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: Afghani and Abduh put reform of Muslim education and thought alongside unity, though Rida's caliphate writings stress state; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Traditional scriptural language is kept by pan-Islamists; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Pan-Islamists treat the Qur'an and sunna as authoritative as they stand; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Pan-Islamism rejects nationalism as divisive and calls for unity across ethnic groups, so it does not favour economic life tied to one national majority.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Pan-Islamism aims at larger Muslim units and rejects division by ethnicity, so merging regions by people is not its aim; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: The movement has no labour doctrine; adherents are split or indifferent.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Pan-Islamists put religious unity over class and see class-based politics as divisive; inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The movement has no economic programme on local services; adherents are split or indifferent.

second-chamber.rationale: The movement has no doctrine on legislatures; the Ottoman-era Senate and the OIC show both forms, so it is split.

municipal-property.rationale: Pan-Islamists want property under sharia and Muslim unity, not local community ownership; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: They want unity of the Muslim world under a caliph or a common body, not decisions left to local assemblies; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Traditional-family views are strong, and sharia places the duty of support on the man; inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: The movement does not address drug approval; adherents are split or indifferent.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The movement does not address ageing research; adherents are split or indifferent.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Their pro-state, sharia-based outlook favours oversight of payments; inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: Their pro-state, sharia-based outlook gives anonymity little support; inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: The caliphate model of Rashid Rida puts the individual under sharia and the community; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The movement rests politics on Islam as a whole way of life, spiritual and worldly, under sharia.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: They favour one Muslim polity with strong central authority, so regional powers would be delegated; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: The movement does not address genetic engineering; adherents are split or indifferent.

dense-cities.rationale: The movement does not address urban form; adherents are split or indifferent.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Pan-Islamism puts religion ahead of ethnicity and nation as the basis of solidarity.

racial-pride.rationale: Pan-Islamism rejects ethnic and national pride as divisive and grounds identity in faith.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Its core cause was resisting European domination, a defensive stance, and the OIC charter commits to peaceful settlement; inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Pan-Islamism bases unity on religion rather than ethnicity or nation, so a shared language does not make a nation for it.

communal-electorates.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its treatment of the Muslim community as a distinct political body, which fits community-based representation.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Afghani's Al-Urwa al-Wuthqa and later pan-Islamists portrayed European powers as working to divide and subjugate Muslim lands, the grievance that motivated the movement.

free-public-college.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the OIC charter's commitment to education and development and from the Islamic value placed on seeking knowledge.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no common view on environmental tax instruments.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Islamic doctrine of humans as stewards of the earth, which implies a duty to hand it on undamaged.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between valuing women's distinct role and rejecting gender as a basis for weighting views.

arms-reduction.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a movement born of resisting imperial power, which tends to favor Muslim strength over reducing arms.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed; the OIC charter sets out consultation among states but says nothing on secret treaties.

capital-controls.rationale: Not addressed; inferred only that adherents want economic independence from foreign powers, which could cut either way on capital flows.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; union under a caliphate suggests central authority but says nothing on armed groups; split.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Pan-Islamists see defence of Muslim lands and the ummah as a duty, and Afghani and Rida called Muslims to resist European powers.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Not a pan-Islamist concern; the movement has no stated labour-relations position.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's economic aims are unity and independence rather than welfare design.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed by the movement, and the OIC charter sets no fiscal rules; split.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Pan-Islamism opposes foreign domination and the OIC charter commits to socio-economic development of member states; inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Pan-Islamists sought to unite or reform existing states, not smash them; Khomeinist revolutionary variants are excluded from scope, so split.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Pan-Islamists look to a single Islamic order grounded in sharia rather than a free choice of economic systems; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed by pan-Islamism; no basis for either answer.

sacred-nation.rationale: Pan-Islamism rejects nationalism as divisive and places loyalty in the ummah, so the nation is not the sacred community.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no basis for either answer.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Pan-Islamists blamed European powers for exploiting Muslim lands, so exploitation of poorer regions by a centre is a familiar charge; the internal form is inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Afghani and Rida appealed to Islam as a universal faith with fixed principles, which fits a shared human nature, though they did not state it; inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: Not addressed; the movement offers no position on public media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Pan-Islamists hold Islam to be the final true religion, the basis of Muslim unity, so they would not treat all religions as expressing one truth; inferred from their Islam-based unity programme.

farm-price-support.rationale: Farm policy was never a pan-Islamist concern; inferred only from general Islamic welfare ideas, with no documented position on price guarantees.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Not a stated plank; inferred from the emphasis on Muslim strength against foreign domination, which makes unilateral disarmament by a Muslim state unlikely to be favoured.

workers-own-party.rationale: Pan-Islamism puts religious solidarity above class divisions, so a separate class party fits poorly; inferred from that, not stated.

ban-fgm.rationale: The movement never addressed FGM and Muslim scholars are divided on it; the OIC charter backs women's rights generally, but no position is documented.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Classical sharia, which pan-Islamists want to shape public life, gives women property rights but fixed, often smaller inheritance shares than men; inferred from the sharia commitment.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Language naming is not a pan-Islamist issue; the movement stresses Muslim unity over linguistic identity, so it is indifferent. Inferred.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the preference for state and sharia-guided public authority over purely private litigation.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Not addressed; pan-Islamists look to ulama, shura and the caliphate for lawmaking rather than tribal chiefs. Inferred from Rida's shura and sharia views.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not a documented concern; inferred from Islamic stewardship ideas and the acceptance of sharia limits on individual liberty.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the sharia commitment: Islamic law fixes penalties for defined crimes rather than leaving them to judges, though repeat offenders are not specifically discussed.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; the movement defends Muslim minorities and migration within the Muslim world, so a language requirement is neither central nor opposed. Inferred.

missingStatements.text: Muslims across the world should be united under a single Islamic state or caliphate.
missingStatements.rationale: The defining aim of pan-Islamism is to unite Muslims under one Islamic state, often a caliphate, as Rida urged in his work on the caliphate.

missingStatements.text: The state should treat the Muslim community, not the nation, as the primary object of political loyalty.
missingStatements.rationale: Pan-Islamism makes the ummah, rather than ethnicity or nation, the focus of allegiance and mobilisation.

missingStatements.text: Foreign powers should not rule or dominate lands inhabited by a religious community.
missingStatements.rationale: Anti-imperialism drove Afghani's Al-Urwa al-Wuthqa and Rida's call to expel European influence.

notes: The movement is a unifying political aim more than a full program, so many economic and social answers are inferred. Adherents split between a caliphate and looser cooperation, between Sunni and Shia versions, and between state-sponsored forms such as the OIC and revolutionary ones.
